name: Radical simplification of what is already there
thesis: ERIS already has the right objects, routes and a working permissions model; what defeats a newcomer is that every page shows everything to everyone, the shell buries content under a 700px navigation card on phones and tablets, and the one long form is a mouse-only pixel canvas. This direction keeps the five destinations, every backend object and every route, and instead removes: each page is cut to the single job it does for the role looking at it, every list becomes a card list below 768px and a priority-column table above it, rail+detail pages become drill-in list-detail below 1024px, the GISA canvas becomes a section hub with a scroll-spy form, autosave and a read-only review mode, every state gets one plain-language label with a 'what happens next' sentence generated from the existing waitingOn() model, and every irreversible action goes through one confirm sheet that also carries the note. Nothing is renamed on the backend; the migration is six phases of mostly layout and component work (about 49 working days) that beats every live baseline: phone content start 700px -> ~104px, technical form 11.1 screens -> per-section pages under 1.5 screens, canvas 532px -> fluid, 120 small tap targets -> 0 on coarse pointers.

principles.name: One job per page, one primary action per state
principles.statement: Every page states the job in its title and shows only the data needed to do it; the role's single next action is a 44px primary button in a fixed place (the Next-step card on desktop, the sticky bottom bar on phone). Everything else is secondary text, behind 'Details', or gone.

principles.name: Content first on every device
principles.statement: Navigation never sits above content. Phone: top bar + bottom tab bar + drawer. Tablet: 64px icon rail. Desktop: collapsible sidebar. Page content starts within 104px of the top on a phone and 72px on an iPad, on every route including maps.

principles.name: Cards below 768, tables above, drill-in below 1024
principles.statement: One ResponsiveList component renders the same row model as a card list below md and a priority-column table from md up (P1 always, P2 from lg, P3 from xl). One ListDetail scaffold renders list and detail side by side from lg and as list -> full-page detail with a back bar below lg. No table ever scrolls horizontally on a phone.

principles.name: Plain words, one per object, with the next step spelled out
principles.statement: Every state code maps through one label function to a phrase a Caltrans newcomer understands, and every status chip is followed by who holds it and what happens next. Raw enums, ids-as-names, 'User #7' and 'Office NORTH' never render. Labels change; backend names, routes and the state machine do not.

principles.name: Forms save themselves and read like a checklist
principles.statement: The technical form (Submission/GISA) is a hub of verb-named sections with Not started / In progress / Complete status, each section a single-column page with autosave, unit suffixes, explicit tri-state radios and inline hints; reviewers get the same sections rendered as summary lists, never disabled inputs.

principles.name: Nothing irreversible on one click, nothing vanishes silently
principles.statement: Delegate, Assign, Submit, Approve, Return, Finalize, Publish, Disable open one ActionConfirmSheet that names the target, states the consequence and carries the note; success is a persistent notice that names what happened, and the item stays visible in a 'Recently handled' group instead of disappearing.

navigation.model: Three-tier adaptive navigation with the same role-scoped destination set on every device (max five top-level items per role plus More). Groups: Work (My Work), Records (Incidents, Assessments, Event Groups), Map (Mission Center route, relabelled 'Map'), Tools (Terrain tools), Admin (Users, Road Inventory), Account (avatar menu). AppShell becomes a React Router layout route so the shell persists and hosts shared state (nav collapse, density, access-denied notice, help panel). The header carries: ERIS mark (link to '/'), page title/breadcrumb, Help (same slot everywhere, WCAG 3.2.6), avatar menu (name, humanized roles, theme, density, Settings, Sign out). Role codes never appear.
navigation.desktop: >= 1280px (xl): left sidebar 240px with icon + label, grouped; collapsible to 64px icon rail, preference persisted in UiSettingsContext. Active item filled with --brand. Count badge on My Work (items waiting on me). Header 56px, sticky; sidebar sticky under it using a --header-h variable measured by ResizeObserver (no magic 82px).
navigation.tablet: 768-1279px (md, lg): permanent 64px icon rail with 10px labels under each icon (min 44px targets), no expanded sidebar by default (expandable to 240px on demand at lg, auto-collapses on navigation). The stacked 'Navigation' card is deleted, so content starts at ~72px. Workspace pages (Map, Terrain, form sections) get main = calc(100dvh - header).
navigation.phone: < 768px: 56px top bar (ERIS mark, page title, Help, avatar) + 56px bottom tab bar with the role's first four destinations and 'More' (opens a bottom sheet with the remaining items, Settings, Sign out). Drawer (slide-in, focus-trapped) also available from the mark for the full grouped list. Bottom bar hides while a form input is focused (keyboard) and inside full-screen map/terrain modes. Content starts at 56px; page title lives in the top bar so the first card is visible at 104px.

navigation.rationale: The brief measured the stacked navigation card as the single biggest cost on every phone and tablet page (content at 700px on both), and NN/g's hidden-navigation data argues against a hamburger-only fix on tablets, so the rail is visible from 768px and the phone gets a bottom bar (Material/HIG guidance in brief-research). Keeping the current routes and section grammar means zero backend or deep-link changes and lets the existing SidebarNavigation/useNavSections code be reused inside the drawer, rail and sidebar. Relabelling Mission Center as 'Map' and Terrain Cross Sections as 'Terrain tools' answers the coordinator's 'where is the map' confusion without touching the URL. Per-role sets are capped at five because Apple HIG and the research both warn against more, and Admin's firehose becomes opt-in because My Work must mean 'mine'.

touchAndDensityRules: Global floor 24x24 CSS px with 8px spacing (WCAG 2.5.8); under @media (pointer: coarse) every button, row action, chip, checkbox, tab, map control and tile action is at least 44x44 px (hit area via padding, not glyph size).

Row density: Comfortable 48px (default when pointer: coarse), Default 40px (fine pointers), Compact 32px (fine pointers only, never offered on touch); persisted per user in UiSettingsContext; changes row height, cell padding and chip size only.
Text floor 12px (chips 12px, body 14px, form labels 14px); the 9-11px overlay/legend text in the terrain and scene components is raised to 12px.

No hover-only affordances: links underlined, selected states use border + background + aria-current, tile actions always visible on hover:none devices, tooltips replaced by visible hint text or tap-to-open popovers.

No nested vertical scroll regions inside a scrolling page below 1280px; maps and 3D scenes get a fixed height and require a two-finger or explicit 'Enable map gestures' tap on coarse pointers to avoid scroll traps.
Bottom bars and sheets respect env(safe-area-inset-bottom); the phone bottom tab bar hides while an input is focused.
Reflow: no two-dimensional scrolling at 320px width except inside maps and opted-in wide tables (which show a visible cut-off and a column picker).
Never set position or z-index on the global .esri-view class; containers size the view and a single z-index scale is used for sheets, dialogs and drawers.

statusLanguage.label: New report - waiting for coordinator
statusLanguage.nextStepCopy: Your district coordinator reviews the report and decides whether GeoTech needs to assess it.

statusLanguage.label: Waiting on reporter
statusLanguage.nextStepCopy: The coordinator asked for corrections to: <fields>. Once the reporter updates them, triage continues.

statusLanguage.label: Accepted - with <office name>
statusLanguage.nextStepCopy: The office chief delegates the assessment to a branch chief.

statusLanguage.label: With branch chief - awaiting engineer
statusLanguage.nextStepCopy: The branch chief assigns an engineer to visit the site.

statusLanguage.label: Engineer <name> - assessment in progress
statusLanguage.nextStepCopy: The engineer completes the technical form and submits it for review.

statusLanguage.label: Closed
statusLanguage.nextStepCopy: No further action. Closed at triage (<decision>) or after the assessment was finalized.

statusLanguage.label: New (shown as small text after the stage)
statusLanguage.nextStepCopy: Not shown as a chip; the stage chip carries the meaning.

statusLanguage.label: In progress (small text)
statusLanguage.nextStepCopy: See the stage chip.

statusLanguage.label: Accepted - assessment required
statusLanguage.nextStepCopy: Creates an Assessment and sends it to <office name>.

statusLanguage.label: Closed at triage - no assessment needed
statusLanguage.nextStepCopy: The report is kept for the record; nothing else happens.

statusLanguage.label: Sent back to reporter
statusLanguage.nextStepCopy: The reporter is asked to fix <fields>; the report returns to your queue when they do.

statusLanguage.label: Closed as duplicate of #<id>
statusLanguage.nextStepCopy: The report is linked to the original and closed; nothing is deleted.

statusLanguage.label: To delegate
statusLanguage.nextStepCopy: The office chief delegates to a branch chief, or assigns the engineer directly.

statusLanguage.label: Needs an engineer
statusLanguage.nextStepCopy: The branch chief assigns an engineer; adding a reviewer now avoids a blocked review later.

statusLanguage.label: Draft - engineer working
statusLanguage.nextStepCopy: <Engineer> completes the technical form and submits it for review.

statusLanguage.label: Submitted for review
statusLanguage.nextStepCopy: <Reviewer names> approve it or return it for revision. If no reviewer is assigned, a chief must add one.

statusLanguage.label: Returned for revision
statusLanguage.nextStepCopy: <Engineer> addresses <reviewer>'s comment (shown above) and resubmits.

statusLanguage.label: Approved - to finalize
statusLanguage.nextStepCopy: The office chief finalizes the assessment record.

statusLanguage.label: Finalized
statusLanguage.nextStepCopy: Assessment complete. The incident stays open until the engineer closes it.

statusLanguage.label: Draft
statusLanguage.nextStepCopy: Continue the form; it saves automatically.

statusLanguage.label: Submitted
statusLanguage.nextStepCopy: Read-only while reviewers decide.

statusLanguage.label: Approved
statusLanguage.nextStepCopy: Read-only record; download the PDF.

statusLanguage.label: Returned for correction
statusLanguage.nextStepCopy: Fix the sections the reviewer named and resubmit.

statusLanguage.label: Open / Closed / Archived
statusLanguage.nextStepCopy: Open: new reports can be attached. Closed: no active incidents remain. Archived: legacy record kept for history.

statusLanguage.label: Nobody assigned yet
statusLanguage.nextStepCopy: A person in this role has not been assigned; an admin or chief needs to assign one.

statusLanguage.label: Consulted
statusLanguage.nextStepCopy: You can read this assessment; no decision is needed from you.

risks: Autosave on web vs offline drafts in the mobile app for the same Submission can conflict; mitigate with updated_at precondition on PATCH and a 'Newer changes exist - reload' notice.

The technical form restructure is the largest single change (1,335-line page); keeping card bodies intact and flagging edit/review modes reduces but does not remove regression risk in the data dictionary mapping.
The dual submit/review state machines require the flagged backend sync; without it the engineer journeys stay blocked regardless of UI.

Reviewer identity is assignment-based while the legacy REVIEWER role still exists; My Work must query assignments for the viewer, or reviewers with only the legacy role see an empty queue (copy explains it).
ArcGIS SceneView on older iPads (WebGL2, 6 GB RAM guidance) - the on-demand gate and 2D fallback must be tested on real devices.
Bottom tab bar and iOS keyboard/safe-area behaviour needs device testing; fall back to hiding the bar on input focus.

Scroll-spy plus sticky index on iPad Safari can jitter with dynamic content heights; use IntersectionObserver and fixed section anchors.
WCAG 2.2 AA verification effort (three themes, chip contrast, keyboard map equivalents) is easy to underestimate; budgeted in Phase 5 but should run continuously.
